articles.title: Holly Throsby: ‘I was proud to not make a breakup album’
articles.summary: The writer and musician on returning to music, finding herself, and why right now is a terrifying time to be an artist. Holly Throsby does not enjoy having her photo taken. There’s even a song on her new album about it.
body: Walking along various bush tracks is a daily ritual for Throsby. A sense of nature gently pervades her seventh album, Normal Magic. It is in the imagery of sparkling water and swims; gardens and birds; bushfires and wind and rain on the roof. The album itself feels like the breaking of a drought: her first solo record in nine years. In the intervening time, she moved to the New South Wales south coast, had her second child, wrote her third novel, and recorded and toured a second album with Seeker Lover Keeper, her collaborative project with Sarah Blasko and Sally Seltmann. She has hardly been idle.

And yet, at 47, she says “there are a lot of things, particularly if you have children, that take you away from the work. I sometimes forget that I’m an artist altogether – for long periods, years. I forget that I’m a musician.”

It’s a startling statement from someone who picked up a guitar at the age of eight. “When I was a teenager, I would get home from school and write songs all afternoon, every afternoon, obsessively,” she says. “It’s been nice to reconnect with that side of myself.”

articles.title: Chat to strangers and let your kids be bored: how to embrace a ‘slow September’ – and enjoy life more
articles.summary: The pressure to self-optimise at the start of the new school year can lead to disappointment and burnout. Instead, here are seven ways to slow things down and reap the benefits. It is a hangover from our school days that September can feel like a time for getting back to the grind.
body: One antidote to this drive is to embrace a slower way of living. Rather than always rushing from one activity to the next, we could be enjoying life.

“In the age of digitisation, from work to socialising, we are seeing everything intensify,” says Heejung Chung, a professor of work and employment at King’s College London. “But by doing everything, we’re also creating a culture where it’s seen as normal. So you are not only creating a standard for yourself, but for everyone else as well. There is a creeping set of collective expectations that we can do everything, especially women, and we need to change it.”
So say “no” to self-optimisation this September, and instead embrace these practical ways to slow everything down – from work to parenting.

More often than not, we feel as though we don’t have enough time to converse with strangers in our daily lives, whether that be the woman next to you at the bus stop or the barista making your coffee. Yet taking the time to mindfully have a conversation with someone we don’t know has tangible benefits.

articles.title: Wide-legged trousers for men are having a moment. Just ask Gary Neville
articles.summary: Neville may have been mocked for wearing them on Monday Night Football, but he is actually bang on trend. From Kylian Mbappé’s World Cup style to Erling Haaland’s hair tie, football has had many viral fashion moments in 2026.
body: Perhaps the one that speaks to the fashion crowd, and a larger debate happening in menswear right now, is Gary Neville being mercilessly teased on Sky Sports’ Monday Night Football for sporting wide-legged trousers.

As a producer played Baggy Trousers, by Madness, Neville’s chino-style, wider-legged black slacks were mocked by fellow pundit Jamie Carragher, who compared Neville to Frank Worthington, the forward from West Yorkshire whose dandyish off-pitch style raised eyebrows in the 1970s.

“I went shopping in London,” Neville explained as Carragher jogged along to the Nutty Boys’ hit. “This guy styled me. I think they’re pretty cool, you know.” He predicted that Carragher would be wearing a pair soon.
Neville seems to be on to something. Because as far as the cut of your trousers goes, girth is greater.

body: We're highlighting the small changes—from useful new gadgets, to fresh productivity techniques, to efficient hacks—that are improving our lives on a weekly basis.

If you've ever left a work meeting thinking, "wait, am I supposed to file the TPS reports, or is it Gary's week?" consider Conversate. I don't multi-task well, so listening while taking notes can be difficult. Conversate solves that problem.

When the meeting is over, you can check out a summary of what was discussed, and Conversate will highlight anything that looks like a task for you. You can then take those tasks and migrate them to your glasses' to-do list with a click, so you have a checkable list of action items floating before your eyes whenever you want it.
I realize that all of these functions could be done with a number of smart phone apps, but with Conversate, you keep your phone in your pocket—much more unobtrusive.

articles.title: Steal My Food Itinerary: A Long Weekend in Upstate New York
articles.summary: I love New York City in the summer, especially this past one, but I grew up in the shadow of the Rocky Mountains. I’m in my late 20s, I rock climb, and I live in Brooklyn, so of course I have an upstate New York itinerary for you. My partner’s mom’s partner (yes) has a
body: Heading upstate this fall for autumn hikes and apple picking? Don’t sleep on all of the farm-to-table restaurants that the region has to offer.

When I tell people in the city about my trips upstate, they’re often surprised to hear me gush about the restaurants. And while I think you could make all your meals (the bounty at the farm stands and markets make cooking very dreamy up there) and still have a great time, I can also strongly make the case for a dining-focused trip. Here’s where to go.

If you’re heading up from the city, there are a few transit options (a bus from Port Authority to New Paltz or Kingston, the Metro North to Poughkeepsie, Amtrak to Hudson), but you’ll want a car to get around once you’re in the Catskills. I journey upstate via a car, which we pick up in New Jersey; that means that I get to grab Corner Slice’s massive, pillowy garlic knots as a pre-trip snack. If you find yourself in the area, I recommend you do the same.

articles.title: Aaron Esh and AllSaints Fêted a New Era in East London
articles.summary: Last night, Aaron Esh—and generations of libertines old and new—brought the legendary British high street brand back to its roots with a ravey launch party.
body: Last night, designer Aaron Esh—and generations of libertines old and new—brought the legendary British high street superbrand AllSaints back to its roots. Esh, now the chief creative officer, hosted a party at the store’s Jacks Place location in the historic Spitalfields, East London, celebrating his inaugural collection.

Friends of the brand and those from Esh’s world, musicians, models, artists, and stylists gathered for the party—many already wearing the slim silhouetted denims, sinewy slip dresses, luxe leather and suede details from the fall 2026 collection. A born and bred Londoner and graduate of Central Saint Martin, the evening—just like his own eponymous label and the new vision for AllSaints—reveled in the city’s cool, contemporary British culture codes. Installations around the store showcased the striking campaign as shot by Alasdair McLellan, styled by Katy England, and art directed by Jamie Reid.
points: Last night, Aaron Esh—and generations of libertines old and new—brought the legendary British high street brand back to its roots with a ravey launch party.

articles.title: 41 School Lunch Ideas That Deserve an A++
articles.summary: Freezer-friendly sandwiches, thermos-ready soups, and more easy school lunches for busy weekdays.
body: Packing school lunches five days a week is the ultimate test of emotional resilience. You think you have a great idea; you send the kiddos off to the bus stop…and the sandwich comes back half-eaten—or worse, traded for a Twinkie. Luckily, we have a batch of school lunch ideas that won’t leave you resorting to too many packets of Goldfish crackers and fruit gummies. Think make-ahead quesadillas, cold noodles, freezer-friendly handhelds, and plenty of snacks and treats to round out the lunchbox.

Some, like our miso-spiked take on PB&J and canned-tuna onigiri, take familiar lunch staples in a new direction. Others, including Jamaican beef patties and chicken quesadillas, can be prepped ahead so weekday mornings require little more than packing and going. Whether you’re looking for kids’ lunch ideas that can be eaten cold, leftovers that travel well, or something besides another sandwich, you’ve got options below.
points: Freezer-friendly sandwiches, thermos-ready soups, and more easy school lunches for busy weekdays.

articles.title: On the Road With Hilary Duff
articles.summary: Before Hilary Duff embarks on the international leg of The Lucky Me Tour—kicking off in Ireland this weekend—she shared some intimate snapshots from her summer on the road.
body: Hilary Duff didn’t know quite what to expect when she dropped Luck… or Something, her first album in nearly a decade, earlier this year. While the 38-year-old never exactly stepped out of the spotlight, she’s spent the last few years focused on acting jobs and raising four kids with her husband, singer-songwriter-producer Matthew Koma. Having spent her teen years touring the world and dropping platinum albums before she could legally drink, Duff considered whether fans would follow her into this new musical chapter.

“I operate from a place of, ‘Do people still care about me? Does anybody even remember that I used to make music?!’” Duff tells Vogue. “That’s the barefoot Texas girl in me who still feels like I kinda have to fake it till I make it.”

articles.title: All the Best Looks From the 2026 Venice Film Festival
articles.summary: As the 2026 Venice Film Festival kicks off this week, all eyes will be on the red carpet—with the likes of George and Amal Clooney, Claire Foy, and Robert Pattinson arriving in the Italian city. See all the best fashion from Venice Film Festival so far.
body: Red carpet lovers, it’s your lucky day: The 2026 Venice Film Festival has officially arrived.

The film roster for this year’s festival has plenty of buzzy projects to take in: Among them is Martin McDonagh’s Oscar-tipped black comedy Wild Horse Nine; Lance Oppenheim’s Primetime; a Robert Pattinson-led portrait of To Catch a Predator host Chris Hansen; and Bunker, Florian Zeller’s marital drama starring Penélope Cruz and Javier Bardem.

Better year, however, is what all of these A-listers will be wearing on the step and repeat for the splashy premieres. This is, after all, the festival that last year offered the first glimpses of new-era Chanel, Dior, Versace and Bottega Veneta before their respective runway debuts, and which has given us Lady Gaga’s feathered Valentino couture gown in 2018 and Zendaya’s wet-look Balmain dress in 2021, among other standout moments.
